curation agent:
⏺ summer_olympics_hosts_1960_2020 staged — ready for audit

  Original concept (no seed match) targeting the empty temporal query category. All cycles 1+2+3 lessons
   applied upfront.

  - 1 master article ("Summer Olympic Games") for universe

  1. 1972 Munich → "West Germany" (politically-current at the time; Germany was divided 1949-1990)
  2. 1980 Moscow → "Soviet Union" (USSR existed 1922-1991)
  3. Tokyo 2020 row Year=2020 (IOC-official designation; physically held 2021 due to COVID-19)
  4. 1964 Tokyo (93) and 1988 Seoul (159) use actually-competed counts where article distinguishes from
  entered-NOC counts (94 entered Tokyo, 160 entered Seoul)

  - All 17 source URLs in Roles: block

What passes:
- Local table mechanics: 16 rows x 5 columns; Year values are exactly 1960, 1964, ..., 2020; duplicate count for primary_key=(Year) is 0; CSV header matches draft.columns; column_types cover exactly the five columns; source_count=17 equals len(source_urls).
- Category and operation fit: query_category=temporal and operation_type=filter match the stated WHERE year BETWEEN 1960 AND 2020 shape. The table is not doing partitioned K-selection; it is an exhaustive temporal slice over a source-defined Summer Olympic Games universe.
- Source-universe fit: the Summer Olympic Games master article lists the 1960-2020 editions in order with host city, host country, dates, and nations, and marks Tokyo 2020 as a 2021-held edition. Staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games, List of Summer Olympic Games table, lines 700-731 and postponement note at lines 770-771.
- Historical country naming is supported: the 1972 page identifies Munich, West Germany with Nations=121 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics, infobox/lead, lines 200-218 and 272); the 1980 page identifies Moscow, Soviet Union with Nations=80 and states the event was held in Moscow, Russian SFSR, Soviet Union (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics, infobox/lead, lines 232-240 and 293-294).
- The documented entered-vs-competed convention is source-grounded. The 1964 page infobox gives Nations=93 while the body explains 94 participated/entered with Libya withdrawing before competition (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics, infobox and participating NOCs section, lines 206-208 and 369-370). The 1988 page infobox gives 160, while the lead says 159 nations were represented at the games; the staged value follows the actually-represented count as documented (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics, infobox/lead, lines 207-210 and 275).
- Recent neutral-team count handling is documented and source-visible. London 2012 uses 206, matching the per-edition body statement and infobox 204+2 convention (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics, lines 257-260 and 320). Rio 2016 uses 207 including IOA/EOR teams (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics, lines 258-262 and 325). Tokyo 2020 uses 206 including EOR/ROC teams, and the official Tokyo 2020 branding despite 2021 dates is explicitly supported (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics, lines 256-258 and 311-312).
- Continent values are reasonable under the documented 7-continent convention: Europe=6, North America=4, Asia=4, Oceania=1, South America=1; Africa and Antarctica are absent for this range.
